divergence_overlap.divergence: The pinned authority performs no check for an overlapping invocation on the same SSL_CONF_CTX. The candidate now refuses EVERY exported entry point that takes a context through one AtomicU8 state and one RAII guard (src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:156-275, acquisition anchors 1606/1651/1743/1801/1837/1886/1916/1948/1993/2050). This closes the concrete interleaving the second rejection named: a dispatch reading prefix/prefixlen while set1_prefix frees and rewrites them, and a free leaving a guard whose Drop stores into released memory.
divergence_overlap.effect: Changes behaviour only for an overlapping or re-entrant call: the authority would proceed, the candidate refuses with the entry point's documented answer. Non-overlapping conforming callers observe no change. Cross-thread use of the wrapped SSL/SSL_CTX remains the caller's obligation.
divergence_overlap.disposition: RECORDED AS A DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE: refuse where the authority would proceed into UB (AGENTS.md sections 17 and 5)

divergence_free.divergence: The authority frees the SSL_CONF_CTX immediately from SSL_CONF_CTX_free. The candidate, when an entry point holds the context, poisons it (CTX_FREE_PENDING) and defers the single release to the holder's RAII guard; later entry points are refused. Free remains void and exactly one release occurs.
divergence_free.effect: The block outlives the free call by at most the remaining in-flight call. No silent leak on a terminating program, and no guard can write into freed memory. If the in-flight call never returns the block is not released, the same liveness premise as any scope-bound resource.
divergence_free.disposition: RECORDED AS A DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE; the rejected alternative (refuse and return) has no in-band signal because free is void

boundaries.contract: `cmd_Protocol` is a `ConfCmdFn` stored as `SslConfCmdTbl.cmd` by the private `commands()` table (`src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:990`, row `:1066`). The only indirect invocation is `f(cctx, value)` in `SSL_CONF_cmd` (`:1473`), reached from `SSL_CONF_cmd_argv` (`:1560` -> `:1616`). `SSL_CONF_cmd_value_type` (`:1643`) reads only `value_type`, never `.cmd`. Preconditions: (1) `cctx` is non-NULL, aligned, live, initialised, and exclusively accessible: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects a NULL `cctx`/`cmd` at `:1522`; provenance is one zeroed `size_of::<SslConfCtx>()` block from `SSL_CONF_CTX_new` (`:1672`); `SSL_CONF_CTX_set_ssl`/`_set_ssl_ctx` (`:1795`/`:1839`) set `ctx`/`ssl` to NULL or live in-crate objects; the shared `&*cctx` at `:1457` is used only for lookup and ends (NLL) before `:1473`, so the handler's writes do not alias a live shared borrow. (2) `value` is non-NULL and NUL-terminated: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects NULL for a typed row at `:1490`; NUL-termination is the public caller contract at `:1489`. (3) No retention of `value`: the handler passes it to `parse_option_list`, which stores only the frame-local flag table in `cctx.tbl` and clears `tbl`/`ntbl` before returning (`:566-567`). (4) Return: `CONF_parse_list` gives 1 when an element matched and 0 otherwise; `SSL_CONF_cmd` maps >0 to 2 and every other value to 0. (5) NULL `cctx` is never delivered (dispatch guard); if it were, the handler would dereference it. A NULL `value` is not delivered either; the handler would answer 0 (CONF_parse_list's NULL arm). (6) Error path: `cctx.tbl`/`ntbl` are cleared on every path; `CONF_parse_list` has its own `guard_ffi`. The slot is private; exclusivity is now a stated precondition of the public SSL_CONF_cmd (# Safety :1489, B46-D1), whose authority documentation states neither (see preconditions).

negative_control.name: ssl::ssl_conf::tests::conf_cmd_dispatch_feeds_a_live_ctx_and_does_not_retain_the_value

new_unsafe_assumptions_note: One production unsafe abstraction: the exclusion guard. It consists of `state` (AtomicU8), `enter_use` (addr_of! + compare_exchange), `InUseGuard::drop` (load/compare_exchange, and the FREE_PENDING arm that calls destroy_and_release), `destroy_and_release`, and the SSL_CONF_CTX_free retry loop (addr_of! + compare_exchange). Every operation carries a SAFETY comment. No signature, exported symbol or #[repr(C)] layout changed; the type is opaque and not repr(C), and the block is allocated through the crate's own seam at size_of::<SslConfCtx>().
boundary_size: Eleven exported C entry points in one file plus the private ConfCmdFn handler cluster and its helpers. The exclusion boundary is one AtomicU8 state machine (`enter_use`, `InUseGuard`, `destroy_and_release`, the free retry loop) that every context-taking entry point crosses; it adds no C-visible symbol. The B46 ConfCmdFn dispatch edge and the B47 helper callees remain the unsafe interiors behind that boundary.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: The confirmation slot, commands table and handlers are private, so no safe Rust caller can install a ConfCmdFn or construct the guard. Every exported entry point is `unsafe extern "C"` and carries a # Safety contract; no safe Rust function in the crate constructs an SslConfCtx reference outside a guarded entry point. The guard is a raw-pointer RAII token, not a value a safe caller can hold after the entry point returns.

entry_point_inventory.coverage_claim: 11/11 exported entry points are classified. Nine acquire the exclusion state directly: the eight mutating entry points (cmd, cmd_argv, finish, set_flags, clear_flags, set1_prefix, set_ssl, set_ssl_ctx) and the read-only accessor cmd_value_type. SSL_CONF_CTX_free acquires when idle and otherwise poisons and defers. SSL_CONF_CTX_new takes no context. No exported entry point that receives a context is left unguarded.

states.name: CTX_IDLE
states.meaning: no entry point holds the context and no free is pending; the zeroed state SSL_CONF_CTX_new produces

states.name: CTX_IN_USE
states.meaning: exactly one entry point holds the context; every other entry point is refused

states.name: CTX_FREE_PENDING
states.meaning: a holder is still live and SSL_CONF_CTX_free requested the release; poisoned: every other entry point is refused

transitions: FREE_PENDING -> released: InUseGuard::drop calls destroy_and_release, src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:277
FREE_PENDING -> any entry point: refused (no transition); IDLE -> freed: SSL_CONF_CTX_free owns the block directly
state.race_closed: If free's CAS loses to the guard's IN_USE->IDLE release, free loops and acquires IDLE itself; if it loses to another free request (FREE_PENDING), it returns and the single holder guard releases. This closes the single-overlap release race only. It does not close a second concurrent free or an entry point racing the release, which remain external caller obligations (criterion_7_2).

guard.drop_behaviour: reads the state; IN_USE -> IDLE on the normal path; FREE_PENDING -> destroy_and_release and return without touching the context again
guard.why_raw: the guard stores the raw context pointer, not a reference, so no shared borrow is live while a handler takes &mut *cctx (B46-H1 shape)

exclusivity_model.reentrancy_rule: Only a successful acquisition creates a guard, and only that guard transitions the state. A nested call cannot clear the outer flag: it fails the IDLE->IN_USE CAS, receives the entry point's refusal answer, and its frame owns no guard. An allocator hook, ex_data callback or provider callback that re-enters any entry point is refused by the same CAS.
exclusivity_model.read_only_decision: SSL_CONF_cmd_value_type is the only exported accessor that borrows the context. It reads flags/prefix/prefixlen, which are not updated atomically as a group: set1_prefix frees the old prefix and then writes prefix/prefixlen as separate stores, and SSL_CONF_cmd_argv updates flags with two read-modify-write stores. A reader that entered between those steps could observe a freed pointer with a new length or half-updated flags. Read-only concurrency therefore could not be established, so the accessor takes the same exclusion guard and answers SSL_CONF_TYPE_UNKNOWN when refused.

criterion_7_2.established_by_this_model: For every non-free entry point, the intra-context precondition is now established by the entry point itself: each caller either acquires the state or is refused, and every exit path (including unwind) releases it. SSL_CONF_CTX_free performs its single release on the immediate path only when it has acquired CTX_IDLE. This covers all 11 exported entry points, but it does not establish the caller's serialisation of free against other calls (see remains_an_external_caller_obligation (c)).
criterion_7_2.remains_an_external_caller_obligation: (a) exclusive use of the wrapped SSL/SSL_CTX: the authority documents (advisory) that one SSL/SSL_CTX must not be changed from multiple threads; the state machine serialises this context's exported API but does not lock those objects. (b) pointer discipline: a C caller must not use the cctx pointer after SSL_CONF_CTX_free returns. (c) free is an external serialisation point: while SSL_CONF_CTX_free runs, no other thread may be inside any SSL_CONF_CTX entry point and no second free may be concurrent. This cannot be enforced in the callee: a second concurrent free, or an entry point racing the release, performs an atomic access on state inside the released block; the void ABI carries no refusal, and an address-keyed check cannot distinguish a freed context from a fresh allocation at the same address without an out-of-band identity or an unavoidable leak. The CTX_FREE_PENDING arm is a best-effort hardening for a single in-flight holder, not a safety guarantee for concurrent use. These are C ABI caller obligations, not hidden crate assumptions.

free_policy.problem: SSL_CONF_CTX_free can run while an entry point holds the context. The rejected guard stored a pointer to a field inside the block, so freeing the block made the guard's Drop write into released memory; a naive 'refuse and return' would leak because the function returns void.

options.option: (a) refuse to free and record the refusal so the caller can retry
options.rejected_because: SSL_CONF_CTX_free returns void. There is no in-band signal, so a C caller cannot distinguish 'freed' from 'refused'. It will normally drop its pointer and leak, or keep it and race; recording the refusal in the context is unobservable through the ABI and is not a contract the caller can act on.

options.option: (b) poison and defer: mark CTX_FREE_PENDING; refuse later entry points; release when the last user exits
options.chosen_because: It preserves the authority's exactly-one-release postcondition without requiring a signal the ABI cannot carry. The block cannot be released while a guard exists, so no guard Drop can write into freed memory; the holder's guard performs the same destroy_and_release exactly once. It also keeps the C caller's existing obligation unchanged: stop using the pointer after free.

behaviour: no holder: SSL_CONF_CTX_free acquires IDLE, releases members and the block once, and forgets its guard before releasing
holder present: SSL_CONF_CTX_free CASes IN_USE -> FREE_PENDING and returns without releasing anything; every later entry point is refused
the holder's guard drops: sees FREE_PENDING, runs destroy_and_release (free_cert_filename, prefix, canames, then the OwnedBuf block) and returns without a further store
another free while FREE_PENDING: returns; the single holder guard still performs exactly one release
guard wins the release race: free's CAS fails with IDLE, loops, acquires and releases immediately
free_policy.consequence: Bounded lifetime extension: the block outlives the free call by at most the remaining in-flight call. No leak on a terminating program; if the in-flight call never returns, the block is not released, which is the same liveness premise as any scope-bound resource. A dangling guard is unreachable. Free nevertheless remains an external serialisation point: a second concurrent free, or an entry point racing the release, is outside the contract and is not made safe by this arm (see criterion_7_2).
